how many wins for the Patriots this year?

let's talk Patriots schedule because Pats fans are asking

at this time last year, I predicted they would play the #2 easiest schedule in the NFL in 2025

by the end of the year, it actually was the #1 easiest, so the prediction that it would be very easy was accurate

last year, the Patriots played just 3 games vs teams that made the playoffs. 3!

#1 fewest in the NFL

not only was it #1 fewest in 2025...

the 3 games vs winning teams was fewest for ANY team in any season the LAST DECADE!

(they went 1-2 in those games)

last year, the Patriots played just 4 games vs teams that made the playoffs

#1 fewest in the NFL

went 2-2 in those games

despite playing an easy schedule, half their wins were by one-score

they went 7-3 (70%) in one-score games

#4 best W-L record in one-score games

they won 77% of games that they trailed at one point!

#2 best W-L record in games trailed

NFL average was 38%

so now, let's discuss the Patriots 2026 schedule

R to @SharpFootball: I project the Patriots to play the #12 easiest schedule in 2026

it may not sound like it, but that is MUCH more difficult than when I gave them the #2 easiest schedule entering 2025

they are projected to play 10 games vs teams with a winning record!

they played only 3 last year

the Patriots will play only 3 teams projected to finish below .500 this year:

Jets
Dolphins
Raiders

everyone else is currently projected at or above .500

the Patriots have the #7 toughest year-over-year increase in schedule difficulty from 2025 to 2026

the biggest criticism of the Patriots last year in building their 14-3 record and making the trip to the Super Bowl was their schedule and how easy it was

that will not be a valid criticism in 2026, assuming their opponents live up to the current expectations of the betting market

while still not above-average in total difficulty, this will be a MUCH harder schedule than the Patriots faced in 2025, and no one will be able to use the "weak schedule" excuse to discredit their record in 2026
I think it's time we have a deep discussion on the Patriots schedule

using last year's records to calculate this year's strength of schedule is great...assuming you don't care about:

- free agency & all the players on new teams
- the 10 new head coaches this year
- the 38 new OCs and DCs this year
- the NFL Draft
- injuries last year that impacted teams
- close game variance last year
- fumble luck, FG luck & other luck factors last year

LeBron James may be taking his talents elsewhere this summer.

At 41, James is an unrestricted free agent, and his options are wide open.

He could retire and ride off into the sunset with one of the greatest careers of all time.

He could return to the Lakers and continue playing with his son, Bronny.

But if he decides to leave LA, things get interesting.

The 2 teams that are most-cited are the Cavs and Warriors.

A return to Cleveland makes sense. This was home for him, and it's where he spent most of his career. 

Now with Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley, Jarrett Allen, and James Harden (pending free agent), the Cavs have built a strong core. And LeBron could supercharge them for one more title run.

But the Warriors somehow make sense too. Once LeBron's longtime rivals, it's no secret he's good friends with Steph Curry and Draymond Green.

And Steve Kerr coached LeBron to a gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics. With potentially Steph, Draymond, LeBron, and Jimmy Butler, it'd be the oldest core in the NBA. But they'd also be must-watch TV.

And then there are some other options.

Earlier this season, ESPN floated the Knicks as a possible destination. New York hasn't been to the Finals since 1999, but LeBron could be the one to get Jalen Brunson and company over the hump.

Or perhaps a return to South Beach, where LeBron could enjoy a season back in Miami with Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro.

Anything and everything is on the table for the 4-time MVP.

And we head into an uncertain offseason where LeBron has a big decision to make.
